ANSWER OF EXELON CORPORATION TO THE MOTION FOR LEAVE AND 
SUPPLEMENTAL PROTEST OF CONSTELLATION ENERGY GENERATION, LLC 
Pursuant to Rule 2131 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy 
Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”), Exelon Corporation on behalf of its 
subsidiaries2 (collectively, “Exelon”) submits this Answer to the Motion for Leave and 
Supplemental Protest that was filed by Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (“Constellation”) 
on April 8, 2026 (“Constellation’s Motion”).   
Constellation’s Motion adds nothing to the Commission’s analysis and should be rejected. 
The motion suggests that Constellation’s limited engagement with one PJM transmission owner 
about one proposed design implies a perverse policy of not only that one utility but of all PJM 
transmission owners.  The motion goes on to imply that Constellation’s one experience somehow 
undermines the justness and reasonableness of PJM’s proposal.  Exelon files this Answer to correct 
any implication that Exelon, the ultimate parent corporation of various PJM transmission owners, 
or those various transmission owners are attempting to prevent large loads, co-located or 
otherwise, and their load serving entities from receiving transmission services in the Exelon 
utilities’ service territories.

I. 
REQUEST FOR CUI//PRIV//HC TREATMENT 
In accordance with section 388.112 of the Commission’s regulations,3 Exelon requests 
privileged treatment for a portion of this Answer containing certain confidential information.  
Exelon understands that the involved counterparty may view this information as competitively 
sensitive and the relevant Exelon utility also treats such information as non-public.  Accordingly, 
good cause exists for the Commission to grant this request for privileged treatment of this 
information.   
Exelon is filing both a public version of this Answer with necessary redactions and a non-
public version of this Answer that contains the confidential information.  The non-public version 
has been labelled “CUI//PRIV//HC” and should be made subject to privileged document protection 
by the Commission.  In accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 388.112(b)(2)(i), a proposed form of 
protective agreement modeled on the Commission’s Model Protective Order is enclosed as 
Attachment B.  To respect the competitive concerns of its customer, the Protective Order has been 
modified to provide additional protections for material deemed “Highly Confidential Privileged 
Material.”  Similar provisions have been included in other approved protective orders in recent 
years.4  Any questions regarding this request for privileged treatment should be directed to the 
undersigned.

ANSWER 
In its motion, Constellation points to a recent communication with a PJM transmission 
owner concerning a large load interconnection request.  Constellation argues that the transmission 
owner “informed Constellation that it would not study Constellation’s proposed design unless 
Constellation agreed to transfer ownership of the ring bus facilities to the Transmission Owner.”  
Constellation does not address the circumstances in which that communication purportedly 
occurred, its formality or finality, or the seniority of the individuals involved.  Nonetheless, 
Constellation argues that this interaction demonstrates the inadequacy of PJM’s proposed 
definition of co-located load.  This is not correct.  <BEGIN CUI//PRIV//HC> 
 
 
 
 
  <END CUI//PRIV//HC> Constellation’s purported experience indicates neither a

DECLARATION OF DAVID WEAVER, PE 
INTRODUCTION 
1.
My name is David Weaver.  I am the Vice President of Transmission Strategy for Exelon
Corporation (“Exelon”).  I oversee the transmission strategy organization with
responsibility for transmission planning and analysis across all of the Exelon operating
companies.  I began my career with Exelon in January 1996.  I have served in various roles
at Exelon in engineering, investment strategy, transmission operations, transmission
planning, substation design, project management, and business planning.  Before joining
Exelon, I worked at Delmarva Power and Light as an engineer in Substation Design and
Transmission Planning.  With more than 35 years of experience in the utility industry, I
also served as chair of NERC’s Planning Committee, President and board member of the
WIRES transmission industry trade group, and board member of the North American
Transmission Forum.  I received my bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from
Drexel University and I am a licensed professional engineer.
PURPOSE OF THE DECLARATION 
2. I am providing this Declaration on behalf of Exelon and its transmission-owning subsidiaries:
Atlantic City Electric Company, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company, Commonwealth

PUBLIC – Confidential 
Material Redacted 
2 
Edison Company (“ComEd”), Commonwealth Edison Company of Indiana, Inc., Delmarva 
Power and Light Company, PECO Energy Company, and Potomac Electric Power Company 
(collectively, the “Exelon Utilities”).   
3. I am responding to the Motion for Leave and Supplemental Protest that was filed by
Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (“Constellation”) on April 8, 2026 (“Constellation’s
Motion”).  In its motion, Constellation points to recent discussions with a PJM transmission
owner concerning a data center interconnection request.  Constellation argues that the
transmission owner “informed Constellation that it would not study Constellation’s proposed
design unless Constellation agreed to transfer ownership of the ring bus facilities to the
Transmission Owner.” <BEGIN CUI//PRIV//HC>
 <END CUI//PRIV//HC> 
EXELON LARGE LOAD STUDY PROCESS 
4. The Exelon Utilities, like others utilities around the nation, have received an unprecedented
influx of requests to interconnect new large loads to serve data centers.  At ComEd, for
instance, over the past two years, there have been many requests, with projected demands of
tens of thousands of megawatts.  The projected demands exceed ComEd’s all-time system
peak, which is to say that they would more than double ComEd’s overall demand.
5. The Exelon Utilities are committed to serving these customers—that is their business and
obligation.  It is what we do.  But it has to be done in a way that ensures that service is safe
and reliable for both existing customers and new customers alike, and thus each request is
subject to study.

PUBLIC – Confidential 
Material Redacted 
3 
6. The details of the study process are evolving, but in general, we have found that it is better
for all concerned to conduct studies in clusters, with projects submitted within particular time
windows studied in synchrony.  To this end, the Exelon Utilities define study “windows”
during which they collect requests from new large loads across their respective service
territories.  Each window has a set deadline for submission, and a new window opens once
the previous window closes. The utility then aggregates the demand schedules, or “ramp
rates,” of all projects submitted during the same window and studies them collectively to
determine the cumulative impact on the transmission system.  Through this analysis, the
utility also identifies whether any transmission or high voltage system reinforcements or
expansions are needed to ensure the safety, reliability, and efficiency of those systems, as
well as the utility’s ability to serve all its customers.  A cluster study includes the
determination of how customers are interconnected to the grid, a planning analysis to identify
any necessary transmission upgrades to maintain reliability, and preliminary engineering,
scope, cost, and schedule to connect customers and complete necessary network upgrades.
Once a cluster study is complete, customers that execute a transmission security agreement
and remain committed to interconnect, have their direct connection needs and any necessary
network upgrades detail engineered and planned for actual construction.  That mode of
analysis is well-established at Exelon where ComEd, for instance, is completing study of
Cluster 2 and preparing to begin Cluster 3.
7. The cluster studies were implemented because one-by-one studies delayed the utility’s ability
to provide customers with critical information about potential in-service dates and sometimes
required repeated re-studies as new projects entered and exited the queue.  The cluster study
process resolves these issues by allowing the utility to evaluate projects together, improving

PUBLIC – Confidential 
Material Redacted 
4 
responsiveness to customers and capturing economies of scale in study and planning 
processes.  This approach also provides a more comprehensive and transparent view of the 
collective impacts of large demand growth.  When multiple projects are proposed in similar 
timeframes, studying them as clusters enables the utility to better assess overall system 
reliability and the interrelationship of nearby loads—insights that cannot be achieved through 
isolated, piecemeal evaluations.  As a result, cluster studies produce more accurate, efficient, 
and forward-looking outcomes for both applicants and the broader customer base.  
8. Because these are studies of service requests for new end users, aspects of their conduct and
their application to those retail service applications are subject to regulation by state utility
commissions.  For example, the ComEd process was the subject of a proceeding at the Illinois
Commerce Commission evaluating proposed tariff amendments to address service to such
loads.   That ICC proceeding recently adopted the process proposed by ComEd.  See,
https://www.icc.illinois.gov/docket/P2025-0677/documents/377910/files/662669.pdf.
9. It is typical that prior to the study being conducted, there will be one or more informational
meetings with the customer to clarify the details of the project to be studied.  These meetings
are an early opportunity for engagement, well before the actual studies occur.  The customer
may seek clarification on the parameters of the upcoming study, and the utility may obtain
information to refine its understanding of the proposal.  Which is to say that the meetings are
a two-way street, each side developing a better understanding of what should be studied.
These meetings do not include policy or legal teams, and are thus not a place where decisions
get resolved.  Where a policy or legal question may arise, those at the meeting will follow an
established escalation path to ensure appropriate review by those with decision-making
authority.

PUBLIC – Confidential 
Material Redacted 
5 
10. The Exelon Utilities use similar informational meetings when other interconnection-related
issues arise.  Because of this, Constellation is very familiar with the process.  For example,
Constellation owns several generation facilities that used to be owned by ComEd, scattered
around the ComEd transmission system, and thus such meetings between ComEd and
Constellation are routine.  Constellation understands the limited role of those who participate
in the informational meetings, but also understands how to escalate an issue to Exelon utility
leadership when a dispute arises.

CONCLUSION 
16. It is troubling to me that the engagement with the transmission owner the Constellation
Motion references is being used to make a legal case.  For Exelon, informational meetings
with customers are never intended to be a place where policy or legal decisions are made.
They are intended in good faith as a place and time where engineers can talk freely so that
studies can be well conducted, and customers can move through the process and come online
as expeditiously and efficiently as possible.  If instead, each party “lawyers up” before each
<BEGIN CUI//PRIV//HC>

Material Redacted

such meeting, I doubt that the meetings will have such free-flowing conversation or that they 
will continue to serve much of a useful purpose.   
17. <BEGIN CUI//PRIV//HC>
 <END CUI//PRIV//HC> 
The suggestion in the Constellation Motion that Exelon utilities, as PJM transmission 
owners, have a policy of denying service based on this issue is incorrect. <BEGIN 
CUI//PRIV//HC> 
 <END CUI//PRIV//HC>

PROTECTIVE AGREEMENT 
 
This Protective Agreement (“Agreement”), entered into this ___day of _______, 20_   by 
and between Exelon Corporation on behalf of its subsidiaries14 (“Exelon”) and ___________ 
(“Intervenor”), shall govern the use of all Privileged, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, 
and/or Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information (“CEII”) Material produced by Exelon 
to Intervenor, or vice versa, in connection with the captioned proceeding before the Federal Energy 
Regulatory Commission (the “Commission”).  Exelon and Intervenor are sometimes referred to 
herein individually as a “Participant” or jointly as the “Participants.” 
 
1. Exelon filed in the above-referenced proceeding Privileged Material, Highly Confidential 
Privileged Material, and/or CEII, as those terms are defined herein.  Intervenor is a Participant 
in such proceeding, as the term Participant is defined in 18 C.F.R. Section 385.102(b), or has 
filed a motion to intervene or a notice of intervention in such proceeding.  Exelon and 
Intervenor enter into this Agreement to govern the use of Privileged Material, Highly 
Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII produced by, or on behalf of, Exelon and/or 
Intervenor in the above-referenced proceeding.  Notwithstanding any order terminating such 
proceeding, this Agreement shall remain in effect unless and until specifically modified or 
terminated by the Commission or a court of competent jurisdiction.  In the event this 
Agreement terminates, the obligations of Reviewing Representatives to maintain the 
confidentiality of Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII 
as provided hereunder shall remain in effect for 18 months following the date of termination.  
 
2. The Commission’s regulations15 and its policy governing the labelling of controlled 
unclassified information (“CUI”)16 establish and distinguish the respective designations of 
Privileged Material and CEII.  As to these designations, this Protective Agreement provides

Agreement, access to such materials by that person shall be terminated.  Even if no longer 
engaged in this proceeding, every person who has executed a Non-Disclosure Certificate shall 
continue to be bound by the provisions of this Protective Agreement and the Non-Disclosure 
Certificate for as long as the Protective Agreement is in effect.22
